latest_findings.description: VSS analysis of /evidence/disk/vanko/surface_physical.E01: no shadow copies found. This may indicate VSS was disabled (T1490: Inhibit System Recovery) or shadow copies were deleted by ransomware (vssadmin delete shadows /all). Check for 'vssadmin' or 'wmic shadowcopy delete' in EVTX EID 4688.

VSS analysis of surface_physical.E01 confirms zero Volume Shadow Copy snapshots exist on the VANKO-SURFACE3 workstation. No pre-incident Security.evtx, MFT, or registry hive recovery is possible via VSS. This means either VSS was never scheduled (typical on Windows 10 consumer configurations), or shadow copies were deleted as part of attacker cleanup. Sigma_hunt found no EID 4688 vssadmin.exe delete shadows in EVTX, so the absence is consistent with VSS never being enabled on this device rather than attacker VSS deletion — but the effect is the same: no shadow copy recovery path exists.

top_findings.description: Five independent artifact sources confirm that Anthony Vanko (PC User / MicrosoftAccount\anthony.vanko@gmail.com) exfiltrated StarkResearch Level 5-8 classified research on 2016-06-30 via a multi-stage operation: (1) EVTX EID 4648 — PC User used steve.rogers stolen credentials against STARK-FILESERVER 34+ times between 2016-06-29T19:51-20:07Z to copy classified files over SMB; (2) MFT — OneDrive classified documents show Copied=True flag (SMB copy from StarkResearch), Dropbox cache files modified 2016-06-30T01:45-01:46Z confirming cloud sync staging; (3) PowerShell history — 216-command session proves PC User bulk-renamed Level 5-8 classified subdirectory contents (Biochemical, Adamantium, Arc Reactor, Armament, Vibranium, Mutant Genome, Carbonadium), archived as vacation photos.7z, then SDeleted all Level 5-8 Classified directories; (4) Prefetch — 7ZG.EXE ran 9 times (2016-06-30T01:17-01:58Z) and SDELETE.EXE ran 10 times (2016-06-30T01:26-01:30Z), corroborating the PowerShell history phase 3 cleanup; (5) Recycle Bin — PC User's entire Dropbox folder (1,908,571,018 bytes ~1.9 GB) was deleted to $Recycle.Bin at 2016-06-30T01:48:48Z immediately after the archive/wipe phase, confirming cloud staging path was destroyed post-exfiltration.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Vanko accessed STARK-FILESERVER legitimately using steve.rogers credentials with authorization, and the file archive/wipe was routine data management
evidence_against_it: PowerShell history shows deliberate renaming of research files using obfuscated names (vacation photos) before archiving — inconsistent with authorized access
SDelete was used (not standard delete) for irreversible secure wipe — indicates anti-forensics intent, not routine data management
defaultprinter covert FTP infrastructure was pre-established June 18 — premeditation excludes authorized one-time access
steve.rogers credentials used via EID 4648 (explicit credential logon), indicating Vanko was not logged in as Rogers — stolen credentials, not delegated access
Dropbox 1.9GB deleted immediately after exfiltration confirms evidence destruction, not routine cleanup

top_findings.description: Four independent artifact sources (Amcache, browser history/disk, UserAssist registry, and ShellBags) converge within 135 seconds (2016-06-18T22:00:37-22:02:52Z) to confirm the covert defaultprinter account established an FTP exfiltration server: (1) Amcache records SmallFTPd binary presence (SHA1: 3f224d...) at 22:00-22:02Z; (2) Chrome browser history shows SourceForge download of smallftpd-1.0.3-fix.zip at 22:00:37Z; (3) UserAssist confirms smallftpd.exe executed at 22:02:05Z; (4) ShellBags confirm defaultprinter actively browsing the Desktop at this time. Temporal co-occurrence across 4 independent sources is a court-grade execution confirmation.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: SmallFTPd was installed for a legitimate file-sharing purpose by an authorized user of the defaultprinter account
evidence_against_it: defaultprinter is a covert account with no business purpose created minutes before the FTP setup (EID Local User Creation at 20:40:54Z)
temp.zip staging archive created and immediately deleted after FTP ran (22:19-22:22Z), consistent only with upload-then-cleanup
defaultprinter account had local admin rights but no corresponding legitimate job role or device assignment

top_findings.description: Four independent artifact sources (disk/browser, file system/$Recycle.Bin, UserAssist registry, ShellBags) converge within 180 seconds (2016-06-18T22:19:09-22:22:09Z) confirming temp.zip was a staging archive created, FTP-transmitted, and then securely deleted: (1) LNK file for temp.zip shows target accessed at 22:19:09Z; (2) RecentDocs registry key confirms temp.zip opened at 22:19:13Z; (3) ShellBag confirms temp.zip visible on defaultprinter Desktop at 22:19Z; (4) Recycle Bin entry shows temp.zip (2,603,690 bytes) deleted to $Recycle.Bin at 22:22:09Z — exactly 20 minutes after SmallFTPd ran. The $R content remains on disk and is recoverable.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: temp.zip was a legitimate personal archive coincidentally created and deleted during the same session
evidence_against_it: temp.zip created inside a covert defaultprinter account session with no legitimate purpose
deletion occurred exactly 20 minutes after SmallFTPd.exe executed (22:02:05Z), matching FTP upload-then-cleanup timing
temp.zip named to appear innocuous but RescentDocs and ShellBag confirm it resided on the Desktop of the covert account specifically created for FTP exfiltration

top_findings.description: Prefetch confirms SDELETE.EXE (Sysinternals Secure Delete — military-grade file wiping tool) executed 10 times in a rapid burst between 2016-06-30T01:26:04Z and 2016-06-30T01:30:52Z (26 minutes after the first 7ZG.EXE archiving run). SDELETE performs DOD-standard multi-pass overwriting that defeats standard forensic file carving. The execution cluster of 10 rapid invocations during the exfiltration window, immediately following the archiving phase, establishes deliberate anti-forensic wiping of staging files. This correlates directly with MFT F-002 (Dropbox cache files deleted 01:45–01:46 UTC) — Vanko archived the classified documents, then securely deleted the originals and Dropbox cache before the system had a chance to sync.

PowerShell ConsoleHost_history.txt (file mtime 2016-07-07T01:38:22Z, 216 commands) proves PC User executed a systematic three-phase classified-data theft: (Phase 1) navigated into Downloads\vacation photos\ and renamed research files to research*.jpg as a cover; (Phase 2) entered Level 7/8 Classified subdirectories (Biochemical, Adamantium, Arc Reactor, Armament, BioChemical, Vibranium, Mutant Genome, Carbonadium) and bulk-renamed all research files to systematic names (L8-Adamantium-gif*.gif, bioresearch*.jpg, etc.) using PowerShell ForEach/rename-item pipelines — preparing them for archiving; (Phase 3) SDeleted the resulting vacation photos.7z exfiltration archive, then securely wiped Level 5, 6, 7 and 8 Classified directories entirely using sdelete.exe and sdelete.exe -s (recursive). The Prefetch-confirmed 7ZG.EXE runs (2016-06-30T01:17-01:58Z) and SDELETE.EXE runs (2016-06-30T01:26-01:30Z) establish this sequence occurred on June 30, 2016.

Prefetch confirms Vanko installed and immediately used 7-Zip and VeraCrypt on 2016-06-29 afternoon UTC — a preparation phase immediately preceding the classified data copy. 7Z1602-X64.EXE (7-Zip installer) ran once at 2016-06-29T16:01:38Z. VERACRYPT SETUP 1.17.EXE (VeraCrypt installer) ran once at 2016-06-29T16:03:03Z. VERACRYPT FORMAT.EXE ran 4 times between 16:12–16:34 UTC creating encrypted volumes. VERACRYPT.EXE ran at 16:12:13Z (first launch). Installation of encryption and archiving tools ~3.5 hours before the STARK-FILESERVER credential theft session (19:51 UTC) constitutes deliberate tooling-up for the exfiltration operation.

STARKSURFACE\PC User (Anthony Vanko's workstation account) used explicit credentials for STARKSURFACE\steve.rogers to repeatedly authenticate against STARK-FILESERVER between 2016-06-29T19:51:07Z and 2016-06-29T20:07:51Z (34+ EID 4648 events). Also attempted STARKSURFACE\lab credentials at 2016-06-29T20:03:33Z against the same server. This indicates Vanko possessed and actively used co-worker Steve Rogers' credentials to access the Stark Research file server — the same server cited in the case manifest for the Level 5–8 Classified data copy.

UserAssist registry key confirms smallftpd.exe was directly executed by the defaultprinter account at 2016-06-18T22:02:05Z (RunCount=1), located at C:\Users\defaultprinter\smallftpd.exe — exactly 84 seconds after downloading the installer via Chrome at 22:00:37Z. This is a user-initiated execution, not a background process.

Browser history (defaultprinter Chrome profile) confirms a focused 28-second FTP server acquisition session: Google search for 'smallftpd' at 2016-06-18T22:00:09Z → SourceForge page at 22:00:14Z → download initiated at 22:00:26Z → file written to C:\Users\defaultprinter\Downloads\smallftpd-1.0.3-fix.zip at 22:00:37Z (67,373 bytes). Chrome was first launched on the defaultprinter profile at 21:59:58Z — this was a fresh Chrome session opened specifically and solely to acquire the FTP server software.

Prefetch confirms 7ZG.EXE (7-Zip command-line archiver) executed 7 times during the exfiltration window 2016-06-30T01:17:50Z through 01:58:22Z, with a preliminary run at 2016-06-29T20:30:36Z. Concurrently, VERACRYPT.EXE ran at 01:12:53Z, 01:40:51Z, and 01:56:46Z; VERACRYPT FORMAT.EXE ran at 01:14:42Z. This execution pattern — repeated archiving cycles interleaved with VeraCrypt volume operations — is consistent with a staged exfiltration workflow: compress classified documents into archives (7ZG.EXE) then encrypt them in VeraCrypt containers before upload to Dropbox/OneDrive cloud sync directories.

Multiple classified Stark Research documents (Level 7, 8, 12) found in Vanko's OneDrive\Documents folder, all flagged Copied=True (M-time older than B-time indicating SMB copy from StarkResearch server), then synced to OneDrive cloud. Includes STARK-TS-Level7-CryoDNA Storage Inventory.docx, Stark_TS-Level8A_CryoDNA.blacklight.docx (20MB), Stark TS-Level 12_Project_Nehemiah 4.docx, and Level 7-formula 88percent ZF 0x17 close.docx (ZF=Zebrafish, created 2016-06-15). First batch copied 2016-04-30; Zebrafish-specific doc added 2016-06-15.

Sigma rules "User Added to Local Administrator Group" (T1078/T1098, medium), "Local User Creation" (low), and "A Member Was Added to a Security-Enabled Global Group" (low) all fired at 2016-06-18T20:40:54-20:40:55Z, confirming the defaultprinter covert account was created AND immediately elevated to local administrator group membership in a single automated sequence — 17 minutes after the NinaResearch research folder was deleted from PC User's Desktop (20:23Z) and 79 minutes before defaultprinter launched Chrome to download SmallFTPd (21:59Z).
supporting_indicators: process: defaultprinter account creation + local admin elevation

top_findings.description: PC User's entire Dropbox folder (1,908,571,018 bytes ~1.9 GB) was deleted to the Recycle Bin at 2016-06-30T01:48:48Z — occurring immediately after MFT-confirmed Dropbox cache deletion events at 01:45-01:46Z. The $R content is not present (purged). This 1.9 GB deletion at 01:48 UTC directly follows the StarkResearch classified file copy window flagged by JARVIS, confirming post-exfiltration anti-forensics cleanup of the cloud sync staging location.

defaultprinter's temp.zip (2,603,690 bytes ~2.5 MB) was deleted to the Recycle Bin at 2016-06-18T22:22:09Z — exactly 20 minutes after smallftpd.exe ran (22:02:05Z per UserAssist). The $R content IS still present on disk and is potentially recoverable. This timing confirms temp.zip was the FTP transmission payload, deleted from the Desktop immediately after the presumed FTP upload to the remote server.

SRUM network usage table parsed via esedbexport. 272 application entries analysed (full dataset). Total outbound across all apps: 50.2 MB. 7 processes exceed 3× median (0.01 MB) outbound threshold. SRUM retains ~60 days of network data — entries for deleted applications indicate potential anti-forensics.

VSS analysis of surface_physical.E01 confirms zero Volume Shadow Copy snapshots exist on the VANKO-SURFACE3 workstation. No pre-incident Security.evtx, MFT, or registry hive recovery is possible via VSS. This means either VSS was never scheduled (typical on Windows 10 consumer configurations), or shadow copies were deleted as part of attacker cleanup. Sigma_hunt found no EID 4688 vssadmin.exe delete shadows in EVTX, so the absence is consistent with VSS never being enabled on this device rather than attacker VSS deletion — but the effect is the same: no shadow copy recovery path exists.

Active interactive user session confirmed on 2016-06-29 evening UTC: 72 LogonType 11 (cached Microsoft Account credential logon for MicrosoftAccount\anthony.vanko@gmail.com) events from 2016-06-28 through 2016-06-30, and 72 LogonType 7 (workstation unlock) events in the incident window, establishing Vanko was actively at the workstation during the period when classified documents were copied (19:51–20:07 UTC). No remote logon source was observed — all sessions were local (127.0.0.1), confirming physical presence. No EID 1102 (Security log clearing) detected — the audit trail appears intact.

Recycle Bin contains two Dropbox-synced files deleted 2016-06-30 01:45-01:46 UTC: "V-Photos" (62,914,560 bytes, Copied=True) and "vacation photos.7z" (35,008,256 bytes, Copied=True) from path $RECYCLE.BIN\S-1-5-21-3739107332-290452467-3466442662-1001\$RK7QVJQ, with Dropbox .attributes ADS. These files were uploaded to Dropbox then deleted from local storage at 01:46 UTC on 2016-06-30, which is consistent with an upload-and-wipe anti-forensic pattern. The 7z archive is a container likely holding classified research.

RecentDocs registry key for defaultprinter profile shows temp.zip was opened/accessed at 2016-06-18T22:19:13Z (LNK: temp.lnk, Target: temp.zip), corroborating the ShellBag entry showing temp.zip on the Desktop at the same timestamp. This is consistent with creating or examining a staging archive before FTP transmission via smallftpd.exe.

Amcache (SHA-1) confirms Tor Browser was installed and actively used on VANKO-SURFACE3. Two distinct firefox.exe versions were recorded: SHA-1 4e477f5413ad65c41d0f60d09af142004d53a858 first seen 2016-05-31T18:30Z and SHA-1 d29808523297286b16ab13e2230e0f7c8a5152b6 (updated version) first seen 2016-06-19T01:34Z — during the incident period 7 days before the STARK-FILESERVER data copy. Tor Browser installation provides an anonymized exfiltration channel for uploading classified materials to web services without leaving a traceable source IP.

Scheduled Tasks (174 tasks extracted) contains no attacker-planted persistence tasks. All off-path non-builtin tasks are legitimate: Google Update per-user tasks, OneDrive Standalone Updater, Apple Software Update, and Dropbox Update tasks. OneDrive update task (version 17.3.6517.0809) corroborates OneDrive was active on the host. Dropbox update tasks (DropboxUpdateTaskMachineCore/UA, registered by STARKSURFACE\PC User) corroborate Dropbox installation. Consistent with an insider-threat actor using interactive logon rather than automated persistence mechanisms.

PC User Chrome history contains only 16 entries spanning 2016-03-12 to 2016-08-08, with zero entries during the primary incident window (June 29-30, 2016). Several entries have no timestamp (NaN), suggesting synced entries from another device. The near-total absence of browsing history for the incident window strongly indicates Chrome history was cleared by the user — consistent with the triple absence of ShellBags, LNK files, and Jump Lists for PC User. PC User browser contains: visit to theintercept.com (2016-04-26 — site publishing leaked classified documents), NetStumbler network scanner download (2016-05-08), Facebook profile photo downloads (2016-06-28T01:18-01:20Z, two days before StarkResearch server access), and AccessData Network License Manager on localhost:5555 (2016-08-08).

ShellBags from the 'defaultprinter' account show it navigated Explorer into C:\Users\PC User\Desktop (FirstInteracted 2016-06-18T22:01:14Z, HasExplored=True), C:\Users\PC User\Documents (22:01:23Z), and C:\Users\PC User\Downloads (22:22:25Z) during the same session that installed SmallFTPd. The defaultprinter account accessed Vanko's personal user profile directories — a covert account browsing a primary user's files is consistent with a staging/exfiltration pivot account.

SRUM: AppId:168 sent 1.0 MB / received 1.2 MB (last record: Nov 03, 2016 11:06:59.231231180). Outbound volume is ≥3× the median for this endpoint (0.01 MB median). Candidate exfiltration — requires corroboration with EVTX network events and memory scan_network findings before labelling confirmed.

SRUM: AppId:1 sent 1.2 MB / received 27.4 MB (last record: Oct 15, 2016 01:00:59.231231218). Outbound volume is ≥3× the median for this endpoint (0.01 MB median). Candidate exfiltration — requires corroboration with EVTX network events and memory scan_network findings before labelling confirmed.
